title: Do positional runes in LP2 hide a message?
question: Do fixed rune positions or line boundaries reveal deliberate ciphertext forcing beyond the effects of physical line layout?
reader_question: Do the first runes of lines, or other fixed positions, hide a message?
summary: One of 21 position and boundary checks flags line initials against a flat shuffle. Reflowing shuffled text by fitted glyph widths makes that apparent anomaly ordinary; six bounded English reading families and the other checks find no supported message.
finding: Independent parsing confirms 12,956 runes on 594 physical lines. The line-initial chi-square is 78.656 against a flat-null mean near 27, but a layout-aware reflow gives p=0.177 in the pinned source and p=0.195 in an independently seeded replay. The other nine position tests and five rejection tests do not clear their gate. Six English-reading families remain below their own best-of-family null maxima; planted controls are recovered. The layout-aware detector has 200/200 power in the two source-planted mechanisms when at least 60% of line initials are forced.
limitations: The width model is approximate and the original typesetter is unknown; the external BabelStone font-width correlation reported by the source cannot be verified because the font file is absent from the pinned checkout. The six message families score English under a bounded keyless transform set. Boundary-rejection tests have little power with only four line-crossing doublets. Planted power applies only to the two specified synthetic mechanisms and fixed phrase; weaker or different forcing remains open. Source message-family nulls were repeated with independent per-family seed states, so sampled extrema differ from the archived serial receipt.
next_steps: Specify any proposed reading rule, target positions, and language before looking at results; compare it with a null that recomputes line breaks and repeats the full candidate search.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited segments of pinned krisyotam_runes.txt; 12,956 rune indices on 594 nonempty slash-delimited physical lines. Hyphen, period, slash and page delimiters retain the source geometry.
scope.procedure: Replay source C-02 Arm A (10 positional histograms), Arm B (six English-scored keyless reading families with within-family best-of-search nulls), Arm C (five position-conditioned repeat/difference checks), the post-hoc width-fit/reflow confound and planted forcing power curve. Independently parse physical lines, verify position and doublet tables, fit widths and reflow with a separate seeded simulation.
scope.parameters: 55 pages; 594 physical lines; 29 runes; source 200,000 Arm A and C null draws per applicable test; source 5,000 layout reflows plus 2,000 independent reflows; six Arm B families and 56,376 source candidate variants; family-specific null replicate counts recorded in replay-armB.json; 200 planted streams per mechanism/fraction and 2,000 synthetic null streams; per-test gate 0.001/21.
scope.exclusions: Other transcripts and page ranges, ornament- or column-defined position sets, language models other than English quadgrams, transforms outside the 232 per-read identity/Atbash/shift/direction/F variants, external font validation, original typesetting software, and any complete LP2 decryption.

review.reviewer: Independent physical-line parser, all ten positional counts and two rejection tables, source replay receipt comparison, width-aware reflow and planted forcing controls

reproduction.environment: Python 3 with NumPy; bundled MIT-licensed source transcription and code; offline.

visuals.caption: The line-initial departure is extreme against fixed positions but ordinary after width-aware line reflow.
Two specified planted forcing mechanisms become reliably detectable at sixty percent of line initials.

pages_note: 55 nonempty transcription pages: LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55. The blank LP2-50 segment contributes no runes.
